rubric.item: Uses independent write and read clocks with different, unrelated frequencies
Checks end to end that no data is lost, duplicated or reordered across the clock crossing
rubric.evidence: C2 only says write data and verify data read; no explicit lost/duplicated/reordered check across the crossing

rubric.item: Checks full asserts after exactly 2^ADDR_WIDTH writes with no reads
Notes that full and empty may assert late (pessimistically) because of synchronizer latency, and checks they are never optimistic
Checks that the pointers crossing domains are Gray coded, with one bit changing per increment
rubric.evidence: Gray-coded pointers are mentioned, but there is no check that one bit changes per increment

rubric.item: Covers resetting the write and read domains independently or at different times
Covers pointer wrap-around
rubric.evidence: Edge case 4: 'Pointer wrap-around: Verify that pointers wrap around correctly.'

rubric.item: Uses independent write and read clocks with different, unrelated frequencies
rubric.evidence: Document mentions two independent clock domains but never specifies different, unrelated frequencies.

rubric.item: Checks end to end that no data is lost, duplicated or reordered across the clock crossing
rubric.evidence: No end-to-end data integrity or ordering check is described.

rubric.item: Checks full asserts after exactly 2^ADDR_WIDTH writes with no reads
rubric.evidence: C3 checks write rejection when full, but never checks for full after exactly 2^ADDR_WIDTH writes.

rubric.item: Notes that full and empty may assert late (pessimistically) because of synchronizer latency, and checks they are never optimistic
rubric.evidence: Synchronizer latency causing pessimistic full/empty is not discussed.

rubric.item: Checks that the pointers crossing domains are Gray coded, with one bit changing per increment
rubric.evidence: C6 checks Gray-code synchronization, but no one-bit-change-per-increment check is stated.

rubric.item: Covers resetting the write and read domains independently or at different times
rubric.evidence: Edge case 1 and C7 cover reset in general, but not independent or staggered reset of the two domains.

rubric.item: Covers pointer wrap-around
rubric.evidence: Edge case 4 mentions pointers approaching max values, but wrap-around is not explicitly covered.

rubric.item: Uses independent write and read clocks with different, unrelated frequencies
Checks end to end that no data is lost, duplicated or reordered across the clock crossing
rubric.evidence: F5 lists a no-drop/no-duplicate invariant as a feature, but no check is defined for it and reordering is not mentioned.

rubric.item: Checks full asserts after exactly 2^ADDR_WIDTH writes with no reads
rubric.evidence: C4 covers a write while full, but no check that full asserts after exactly 2^ADDR_WIDTH writes.

rubric.item: Notes that full and empty may assert late (pessimistically) because of synchronizer latency, and checks they are never optimistic
Checks that the pointers crossing domains are Gray coded, with one bit changing per increment
rubric.evidence: Gray coding is mentioned as a feature, but there is no check that exactly one bit changes per increment.

rubric.item: Covers resetting the write and read domains independently or at different times
rubric.evidence: F6 lists wr_rst_n and rd_rst_n, but independent or staggered reset is not covered.

rubric.item: Covers pointer wrap-around
Checks that the first arbitration after reset grants requester 0 when several requesters are active
Checks round-robin order under continuous contention, with each requester served in turn
rubric.evidence: C2 'Priority should rotate after serving' is vague; no check of each requester served in turn under continuous contention

rubric.item: Checks the grant doesn't change while a burst is in progress even if req changes (no preemption)
rubric.evidence: C1: 'Request during burst should not change'

rubric.item: Checks the grant is released after burst_done and a new arbitration only starts afterwards
rubric.evidence: C4 'Grant should be released after burst_done' does not state that new arbitration only starts afterwards

rubric.item: Checks grant is always zero or one-hot and grant_valid equals the OR of grant
rubric.evidence: C3 'grant_valid should be correct' is vague; no one-hot or OR check

rubric.item: Covers a single requester being granted repeatedly when nobody else requests
Includes burst_done arriving on the first cycle of a grant (one-cycle burst) as an edge case
Covers the round-robin pointer wrapping from the last index back to index 0
Checks that the first arbitration after reset grants requester 0 when several requesters are active
rubric.evidence: C5 only says 'Verify behavior during reset'; it does not say requester 0 wins the first arbitration

rubric.item: Checks round-robin order under continuous contention, with each requester served in turn
rubric.evidence: C2 'verify round-robin order of grants' is generic and does not specify continuous contention with each requester served in turn

rubric.item: Checks the grant doesn't change while a burst is in progress even if req changes (no preemption)
rubric.evidence: Edge case 3 'Preemption during burst lock' is mentioned only vaguely, and no specific check is defined

rubric.item: Checks the grant is released after burst_done and a new arbitration only starts afterwards
rubric.evidence: F3 mentions clearing the grant on burst completion, but no check verifies release and a new arbitration afterwards

rubric.item: Checks grant is always zero or one-hot and grant_valid equals the OR of grant
rubric.evidence: F4 lists grant_valid, but there is no one-hot check or explicit grant_valid == |grant check

rubric.item: Covers a single requester being granted repeatedly when nobody else requests
Includes burst_done arriving on the first cycle of a grant (one-cycle burst) as an edge case
Covers the round-robin pointer wrapping from the last index back to index 0
rubric.evidence: C3 mentions cycling over max and min N, but pointer wrap from last index to 0 is not explicit

rubric.item: Checks that the first arbitration after reset grants requester 0 when several requesters are active
rubric.evidence: C2 only checks grant_valid after reset, not that requester 0 is granted first

rubric.item: Checks round-robin order under continuous contention, with each requester served in turn
rubric.evidence: C3 says grant cycles to each request fairly, but not a clear round-robin order under continuous contention

rubric.item: Checks the grant doesn't change while a burst is in progress even if req changes (no preemption)
rubric.evidence: C6 says a new request before burst_done updates grant, which is preemption, the opposite of this item

rubric.item: Checks the grant is released after burst_done and a new arbitration only starts afterwards
rubric.evidence: C5 only checks grant_valid is false after burst_done, not that a new arbitration starts afterwards

rubric.item: Checks grant is always zero or one-hot and grant_valid equals the OR of grant
rubric.evidence: C7 is vague and does not check one-hot or grant_valid equal to the OR of grant

rubric.item: Covers a single requester being granted repeatedly when nobody else requests
rubric.evidence: No single-requester scenario is covered

rubric.item: Includes burst_done arriving on the first cycle of a grant (one-cycle burst) as an edge case
rubric.evidence: No one-cycle burst edge case is listed

rubric.item: Covers the round-robin pointer wrapping from the last index back to index 0
rubric.evidence: last_idx coverpoint: 'Checks if the round-robin pointer wraps around correctly'

rubric.item: Checks data and the last flag come out in the order they were written
rubric.evidence: No data/last ordering check; C2 is about rd_data vs rd_last under no rd_ready, not order.

rubric.item: Checks full asserts after exactly DEPTH writes and that writes are refused while full
rubric.evidence: C4 and C6 cover full asserting at DEPTH and wr_ready deasserted, but there is no check of exactly DEPTH writes or that writes are refused while full.

rubric.item: Checks rd_valid stays low and nothing is read while the FIFO is empty
rubric.evidence: C7: Simulate empty FIFO and verify that rd_valid is deasserted

rubric.item: Checks fill_level tracks occupancy, including during simultaneous read and write
rubric.evidence: F3/C3 mention fill_level, but C3 says it remains unchanged after write and read; F6 says count stable on simultaneous operation, but there is no explicit check that fill_level tracks occupancy.

rubric.item: Covers simultaneous read and write both when the FIFO is full and when it is empty
rubric.evidence: Simultaneous read/write coverage is generic, not specified at full and at empty.

rubric.item: Covers read and write pointer wrap-around
rubric.evidence: No pointer wrap-around coverage.

rubric.item: Checks behaviour when reset is asserted while the FIFO holds data
rubric.evidence: Reset is only checked after reset (C1), not asserted while the FIFO holds data.

rubric.item: Covers read-side back-pressure (rd_ready low while data is available)
rubric.evidence: The rd_ready bin is described as low when the FIFO is empty, which is not back-pressure with data available; the open question on back-pressure is not a coverage item.

rubric.item: Checks data and the last flag come out in the order they were written
Checks full asserts after exactly DEPTH writes and that writes are refused while full
rubric.evidence: C1 only says wr_ready goes low when writing to a full FIFO; there is no check that full asserts after exactly DEPTH writes.

rubric.item: Checks rd_valid stays low and nothing is read while the FIFO is empty
rubric.evidence: C2 says rd_valid goes low on a read from an empty FIFO, but nothing checks that no data is read.

rubric.item: Checks fill_level tracks occupancy, including during simultaneous read and write
rubric.evidence: C3 covers fill_level updates on reads and writes, and C4 covers simultaneous read/write, but neither explicitly checks fill_level during simultaneous operation.

rubric.item: Covers simultaneous read and write both when the FIFO is full and when it is empty
rubric.evidence: C10 covers simultaneous operation generally, with no full/empty distinction.

rubric.item: Covers read and write pointer wrap-around
Checks behaviour when reset is asserted while the FIFO holds data
rubric.evidence: C5 only covers the initial state after reset.

rubric.item: Covers read-side back-pressure (rd_ready low while data is available)
rubric.evidence: C7 deasserts rd_ready during a write, but does not specify data available; it is too vague.

rubric.item: Checks data and the last flag come out in the order they were written
rubric.evidence: C3 checks read data aligns with write data, but there is no mention of the last flag or of ordering.

rubric.item: Checks full asserts after exactly DEPTH writes and that writes are refused while full
rubric.evidence: C4 says backpressure prevents write when full, but it does not state that full asserts after exactly DEPTH writes.

rubric.item: Checks rd_valid stays low and nothing is read while the FIFO is empty
rubric.evidence: C4 mentions preventing read when empty, but there is no check that rd_valid stays low.

rubric.item: Checks fill_level tracks occupancy, including during simultaneous read and write
rubric.evidence: C5: simultaneous read and write operations correctly affect count; C6 count tracking.

rubric.item: Covers simultaneous read and write both when the FIFO is full and when it is empty
rubric.evidence: Simultaneous operations are covered generally, but not specifically at the full and empty states.

rubric.item: Covers read and write pointer wrap-around
rubric.evidence: C2 mentions wrap around when filled to max depth, but there is no explicit pointer wrap coverage. The coverpoint bins are Full/Half/Empty.

rubric.item: Checks behaviour when reset is asserted while the FIFO holds data
rubric.evidence: C7: FIFO handles reset in the middle of an operation using a random test with reset insertion

rubric.item: Covers read-side back-pressure (rd_ready low while data is available)
rubric.evidence: No check or coverage for rd_ready low while data is available.
